text:
serena: hitting a puzzling TS break in the new edge sample deployed to Cloudflare Workers. consumers using the sample get a compile-time error when they annotate generics on client.generate<>.

serena: minimal consumer snippet (tsup -> worker):
```ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = createClient({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('RW_KEY') })
const out = await client.generate<{ answer: string }>({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'ping' })
console.log(out.answer)
```

serena: build error: "Argument of type '{ model: string; prompt: string; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'GenerateOptions<any>'" and TS says type inference for T failed. weird.

mira: that screams overload + import-shape mismatch. we bundle for edge (ESM) and also ship CJS shims for node. our .d.ts has two overloads: one legacy using any and another generic one using unknown. TS picks the wrong one after bundler transforms imports.

tom: spike: reproducible only when consumer uses moduleResolution: 'bundler' + allowSyntheticDefaultImports: false. with node resolution it works. bundlers rewrite imports so the symbol shape becomes a namespace object and overload resolution changes.

kevin: short-term: add note in edge README recommending either `esModuleInterop: true` or `import * as RI from '@redwood/inference'` then `RI.createClient()` as workaround. we should also ship a tiny `cjs-compat.js` that sets `module.exports = exports.default` to help some bundlers.

mira: long-term: simplify types. remove the dual overloads and export a single strongly-typed generic API surface. e.g. `function generate<T = unknown>(opts: GenerateOptions): Promise<T>` and `createClient` returns typed methods. avoid `any` in exported overloads.

tom: also audit auth/retry wrappers. we have separate overloads for sync/async retry that slip in `any` in one signature; same root cause.

serena: action plan: 1) types PR to collapse overloads and default to unknown, 2) update published `types` entry in package.json to point strictly to dist/index.d.ts, 3) add edge sample CI that builds with moduleResolution=bundler and esModuleInterop=false, 4) add small README note and example tsconfig for Cloudflare/Vercel edge targets.

mira: i'll grep for overload pairs and `= any` defaults, submit a types-only PR. include a tiny repro repo and a CI job that builds the edge sample with esbuild/tsup.

devex-bot: created issue #3988 (dx: edge bundle + ts moduleResolution=bundler causes generic inference failures)

serena: thanks! will test the PR against our sample and downstream consumer that hit this.
